cases.title: No Routes Found PE2 — Ringba (Alaska PPT Filtering)
cases.findings: Root cause: Profit Protection Threshold (PPT) filtering blocks Alaska (+19076005911) routes. Customer tariff $0.0035/min, PPT $0.10/min. Available carriers at $0.04/min and $0.225/min — both blocked by PPT. no_routes_found_with_ppt=true confirmed in TREAT routing response. Initial CDR analysis incorrectly identified missing outbound profile — CORRECTED after TREAT showed PPT is the actual issue. Call Control/TeXML transfers route through app layer, not via assigned outbound profile.
cases.notes: Sensei-assisted deep analysis. TREAT confirmed PPT root cause on 3/5 samples (2 timed out, re-queried). Key lesson: don't rely on CDR outbound_profile_id=null for Call Control transfers — verify routing response data. Response sent to customer — waiting for customer to choose option (adjust PPT vs custom Alaska rate).
cases.response: Sent to customer — awaiting choice: (1) adjust PPT with cost acceptance, (2) escalate to billing for custom Alaska rate.

cases.title: DTMF # Not Working — Adit (Asterisk Payload Mismatch)
cases.findings: DTMF # not forwarded to upstream carrier. Root cause: Asterisk payload type mismatch — Asterisk advertises PT 103 for telephone-event in SDP answer but sends DTMF events on PT 101. B2BUA correctly ignores PT 101 per RFC 3264. Affects ALL DTMF digits, not just #. PCAP confirms 30 DTMF events on PT 101 from Asterisk.
cases.notes: Sensei-assisted deep analysis. PCAP + SDP analysis identified Asterisk config mismatch. Drafted customer-facing response recommending Asterisk config fixes. Sean approved.
cases.response: Response sent to customer — Asterisk dtmfmode=rfc2833 config fix recommended.

cases.title: Outbound Busy Signal Investigation — Ringba
cases.findings: Outbound calls getting busy signal; client's call center says calls never reached them. SIP analysis of 5 call legs shows: initial carrier gateway 503 errors, then 603 Decline from far end, then eventual success on final attempt. The 'busy' = destination actively declining (603 Decline). Carrier gateways returning 503 on initial attempts also concerning. Client uses sequential dialing (tries multiple targets).
cases.notes: Sensei-assisted SIP analysis. 5 UUIDs analyzed. Key finding: 603 Decline from far end = destination rejecting, not network issue. 503 from carrier gateways on initial attempts = pre-routing rejection. Call center may have PBX auto-reject or queue capacity limits.
cases.response: SIP analysis shared — recommend client check PBX/ACD auto-reject rules and queue capacity.

cases.title: One-Way Audio After Call Transfers — HelloPatient
cases.findings: After call transfers, callee cannot be heard (one-way audio). NOT cross-DC — all legs on LV1. NOT new — present yesterday too. B2BUA Opus jitter anomaly: 5500-7100ms reported vs <1ms in PCAP. Multi-codec transcoding (PCMU+G722+Opus) causes FreeSWITCH Opus jitter buffer issues. Dan from internal team handling via ClearFeed. Finding: silent RTP (0xFF) from downstream carrier.
cases.notes: Sensei-assisted deep analysis. PCAP analysis, CDR correlation, codec path investigation. Root cause: B2BUA Opus jitter buffer artifact under multi-codec load. Quick fix: PCMU-only on outbound PSTN connection.
cases.response: Dan handling via ClearFeed. Silent RTP from downstream carrier confirmed.
